key_insight: Vacuum annealing progressively transforms detonation-sprayed NiCrAl coatings from a β-NiAl-dominated lamellar state toward homogenized structures and, at 1000–1100 °C, oxide-containing states.
engineering_relevance: Annealing temperature offers a way to tune coating structure, but higher temperatures increase oxidation and coating–substrate interdiffusion.
method: Deposit NiCrAl coatings by detonation spraying.
Vacuum anneal at 800, 900, 1000, and 1100 °C for 4 h.
Evaluate phase evolution, morphology, interface changes, and surface roughness.
evidence_signal: Ra was 6.0, 5.3, 5.3, and 5.9 µm at 800, 900, 1000, and 1100 °C, respectively; treatment at 1100 °C produced multiple oxides and a heterogeneous transition zone with local microvoids.
watch_item: Structural changes alone do not establish service-performance gains; the abstract reports no adhesion, wear, or corrosion testing.
paper_title: Effect of Vacuum Heat Treatment on the Structural-Phase State of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrAl Coatings
